subject.title: feat: bound transcript reads across replacements

question: Should OpenClaw publish generation-aware raw and visible transcript cursor APIs as a permanent Plugin SDK contract, and accept the accompanying durable generation state now?
rationale: This cannot be resolved mechanically: it chooses a new external plugin contract and determines whether durable transcript-generation state is justified as a core capability rather than a narrow internal optimization.

options.title: Approve a narrow cursor contract
options.body: Accept the raw and visible cursor APIs, but require the additive generation table to use the lazy idempotent ensure path instead of a schema-version bump.

options.title: Keep the optimization internal
options.body: Retain only the bounded active-memory read or another owner-local optimization and do not publish persistent cursor semantics through the Plugin SDK.

options.title: Defer to a scoped design discussion
options.body: Pause the PR until maintainers define cursor ownership, reset guarantees, and the intended external consumers.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow cursor contract
recommendation.body: Accept the raw and visible cursor APIs, but require the additive generation table to use the lazy idempotent ensure path instead of a schema-version bump.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core persistence policy and the public Plugin SDK boundary, with no narrower owner established by the supplied history.
